gaps.sentence: We mustn't miss ___ this exhibition — it ends on Sunday.
It's not worth ___ over spilt milk.
He denied ___ the money, but nobody believed him.

gaps.explanation: can't stand + -ing (also to-infinitive in AmE): can't stand waiting. -ing accepted as standard.

gaps.sentence: It started ___ just as we left the house.
gaps.explanation: start/begin take either -ing or to-infinitive; with continuous or states, 'to' is preferred. Both accepted.

gaps.sentence: When I was a student, I used ___ in shared flats.
gaps.explanation: used TO + infinitive = past habit/state: used to live. (Compare: be used to living.)

gaps.sentence: The box was heavy enough ___ two people.
gaps.explanation: adjective + enough + to-infinitive: heavy enough to need.

gaps.sentence: The hotel offered ___ our room free of charge.
gaps.explanation: offer takes the to-infinitive: offered to upgrade.
